input: Update emergency contact info at my workplace

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: They may need to update just one contact, remove old ones, add new ones, or also update related details like medical info or next-of-kin — this changes how much work is involved.
Knowing who the new emergency contact is (name, relationship, phone) determines what information needs to be gathered before starting.
The process varies hugely depending on company size and type — a large corporate HR portal works differently from a small business with paper forms.
The method of updating (online HR system, paper form, email to HR, in-person visit) determines the immediate next action the user must take.
There may be a deadline driving urgency — e.g., an open enrollment window, a recent life event, or a compliance reminder — which affects how quickly this must be done.
The user may just want confirmation it is submitted, or may need written proof the record was updated — this changes what 'done' looks like.
Some people want step-by-step guidance through the process; others just need a checklist or a reminder of what info to have on hand — this shapes what kind of plan is most useful.

gold.taskTitle: Update emergency contact info at workplace
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to update their emergency contact information on file with their employer.

questions.title: Are you adding a new contact, replacing an existing one, or both?
questions.description: Clarifies the scope of the update — whether this is a simple replacement or a more involved restructuring of emergency contact records.

questions.title: Who is the new emergency contact you want on file?
questions.description: Identifies the person (name, relationship, phone number) the user intends to list, so all needed information can be gathered upfront.

questions.title: How big is your workplace — large company, small business, or something else?
questions.description: Determines the likely HR infrastructure in place, which directly affects what process the user will need to follow.

questions.title: Do you know how your company handles HR updates — online portal, paper form, or email?
questions.description: Pinpoints the exact channel the user must use, which defines the very first action they need to take.

questions.title: Is there a deadline or urgency driving this update right now?
questions.description: Reveals whether this is time-sensitive due to an open enrollment window, a life event, or a compliance prompt, which affects prioritization.

questions.title: Do you need written confirmation that the record was successfully updated?
questions.description: Defines what 'done' means to the user — simple submission vs. obtaining documented proof of the change.

questions.title: Would you prefer a step-by-step walkthrough or just a checklist of what to prepare?
questions.description: Shapes the format and depth of the plan based on how much guidance the user wants through the process.
